title: Quant regression investigation: tiling interference on AWQ kernels
content:
Purpose

Quick working notes for a regression we started seeing in March: AWQ-backed INT8 kernels occasionally show a 10-30% throughput drop on mixed batch-shape workloads compared to earlier AWQ runs. This doc captures the profiling, hypotheses, repro steps, and short-term mitigations. Not a final postmortem.

Context and why it matters

- Customer workloads (concurrent chat + embeddings) created mixed batch-size tails. We rely on AWQ kernels for cost-sensitive models in production. Regression shows up as throughput loss and higher token cost in Dedicated clusters.
- Repro is deterministic on our internal perf harness; failure pattern correlates with specific tiling and micro-batching boundaries.

Observed behavior summary (quick)

- Setup: A100s (40GB), CUDA 12.1, runtime commit 1.23.1 (branch: feature/awq-tiling-optim), model: redwind-13b-instruct (off-the-shelf AWQ quantized).
- Workload: mixed client shapes (1, 2, 4, 8) in a 10k request sample. Mixture: 50% size=1, 25% size=4, 25% size=8.
- Baselines: FP16 kernel (reference) and previous AWQ run from Feb (commit 1.22.0).
- Symptom: median throughput down ~12%, p99 latency increased by ~18% in the mixed shape run. Cold-start unaffected. Single-shape microbenchmarks (pure batch=8) do not show regression.

Microbench numbers (representative)

- FP16 baseline (batch-mix harness): throughput = 420 req/s, median token latency = 32ms, p99 = 90ms
- AWQ (Feb, commit 1.22.0): throughput = 520 req/s, median = 26ms, p99 = 72ms
- AWQ (Mar, commit 1.23.1): throughput = 456 req/s, median = 31ms, p99 = 85ms
- GPTQ (same quant profile) for reference: throughput = 480 req/s, median = 29ms

Hypotheses (ranked)

1) Tiling/packing interaction with mixed batch shapes causes non-amortized memory copies and kernel re-launch overhead. AWQ packing code introduced a tiled path that tries to reuse packed tiles across requests; reuse policy appears to thrash when batch shapes vary.
2) Kernel selection fallback logic (new in 1.23) misroutes some sequences to a conservative kernel that has better numerical stability but worse throughput for long sequences; mismatch triggers more often when tile boundaries align with attention block boundaries.
3) NVMe-backed KV cache flush/eviction timing got tweaked in the same release which means more host <-> device transfers for some edge patterns. This is lower probability but should be considered.

What we profiled

- nvprof/nsys traces for hot path (sampled 1k requests from harness) comparing 1.22.0 vs 1.23.1. Captured kernel durations, memcpy H2D/D2H, and kernel launch counts.
- Internal microprofiler (per-request): time spent in pack(), tiled_kernel(), unpack(), memcopy, and scheduler queueing.
- Perf counters: L2 cache misses, DRAM throughput (nvml), and GPU occupancy.

Key profiling signals

- Kernel launch count per request increased by ~27% in the mixed-shape run on 1.23.1 vs 1.22.0.
- pack() time increased ~3x (absolute small, but frequent). The pack path now does a small memcpy per tile when reuse misses; reuse miss rate ~45% in mixed-run (vs 8% in single-shape).
- DRAM bandwidth utilization spiked during the tail, L2 misses increased modestly. Occupancy roughly similar.

Repro steps (harness)

1) Checkout runtime@commit 1.23.1 and 1.22.0 (for diff).
2) Activate conda env: conda activate ri-bench
3) Run harness script (this reproduces the mixed-shape sample):
   python tools/bench/multi_shape_harness.py --model redwind-13b-instruct-awq --shapes 1:50,4:25,8:25 --iters 10000 --concurrency 64 --profile nsys --out out_1.23.1.qlog
4) Repeat the same on 1.22.0 and compare: nsys stats --report=summary out_1.22.0.qlog out_1.23.1.qlog
5) To capture internal counters: run with --microprofiler and examine /tmp/microprof-*.csv

Quick diffs in runtime to inspect

- runtime/quant/awq/packer.cpp: new tiled_pack path (introduced in commit 1.23). Focus the review on reuse hash policy and lock-free map eviction.
- runtime/scheduler/kernel_selector.cpp: minor policy tweak that prefers numerical-stable kernel on high-variance seq len workloads.

Short-term mitigations we tested (and results)

- Force old packer (env var RW_AWQ_PACKER=legacy): throughput returned to within 2% of Feb baseline. p99 improved. This is a reliable toggle for immediate mitigation.
- Harden reuse hash (use single-threaded test path): reduces pack() miss rate to 10% but increases pack latency per op. Net throughput ~+6% vs 1.23 default.
- Disable conservative kernel fallback (env var RW_KERNEL_FALLBACK=off): small improvement (~3% throughput) but regained p99 tail concerns on long sequences. Not safe for prod without more QA.

Deeper root-cause notes

- The tiled packer does aggressive fine-grained tile eviction aimed at reducing memory footprint. For uniform workloads that amortizes well, but mixed shapes result in high eviction churn because tiles are keyed by (seq_len, slot_size) and our keying did not account for slot aliasing across small batch sizes.
- The reuse map uses a 32-bit truncated hash which increases collisions under the many-small-shape regime. Collisions cause false misses -> re-pack -> more memcopies and kernel launches.

Action plan (next steps, owners)

- Short term (hotfix, <48h): Revert to legacy packer for the Dedicated pool and push a config flag to Hosted to opt-out. Owner: Priya N. (engops)
- Mid term (2 weeks): Implement stronger reuse key (64-bit fingerprint of model+tile dims) and add a small LRU instead of eviction-on-collision. Owner: Diego A.
- Mid term: Add a unit/regression harness focused on mixed-shape sequences (extend multi_shape_harness) to run nightly against mainline. Owner: Hannah P.
- Longer term: Rethink tiled packing policy to be batch-shape-aware at scheduler level (route similar shapes to same worker to increase pack reuse). Owner: eng-serving-runtime roadmap.

Notes on measurement trust and caveats

- Harness uses synthetic prompts and deterministic RNG; real customer distribution may have different reuse patterns. We sampled a few customer traces and saw qualitatively similar miss rates but not identical magnitude.
- Repro on V100 showed smaller effect (likely because memory path and kernel scheduling differs). This indicates CUDA driver/kernel launch semantics interact here.

Open questions

- Does AWQ model layout (per-layer tile alignment) amplify specific hash collision patterns? Need a small instrumented run to capture per-layer tile ids and collision rates.
- Are there any codepaths that can pack lazily (defer actual memcpy until just-in-time) to avoid repeated copies?

Appendix: useful commands and probes

- nsys profile: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --output out_nsys
- query microprofiler (simple): cat /tmp/microprof-*.csv | egrep "pack|tile|kernel_launch" | sed -n '1,200p'
- kernel launch counter (quick): nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o D

- Example harness command for single-shape control:
  python tools/bench/multi_shape_harness.py --model redwind-13b-instruct-awq --shapes 8:100 --iters 5000 --concurrency 64

- Patch references: PR 482 touches packer.cpp. See runtime/quant/awq/packer.cpp#L120-260 for the tiled path.

Housekeeping

- I pushed a small repro artifact to s3://ri-perf/tiling-repro/2025-03-12/ (internal).
- Will create a short demo doc for EngOps runbook to toggle RW_AWQ_PACKER env flag.

If you're triaging this: start by running the legacy packer toggle in staging, capture nsys traces, and upload to the perf channel. I'll coordinate the hotfix revert if we see matching numbers in staging.
